producer_report.summary: The reading check now refuses a boundary word only in a deliverable path or in a `content` acceptance criterion. Title, summary, assumptions, out_of_scope, defaults_applied, the decline/hard/urgent reasons, question, departures and `behavior` criteria are no longer scanned. In reading.rs, `reading_text_fields` became `file_bound_text_fields`, which returns only `content` criteria. `check_boundary_and_repo_files` keeps its name and signature, and the repository-file checks and request-text scan are unchanged. The repair text now says "deliverable path or content acceptance criterion". The module docs and the function doc comments state what is scanned and not, and why: readings are records outside the policy scan, and the writer gets the word list and runs the scan (D73). D153 and a CHANGELOG bullet record the reason, the alternatives and the cited refusals. Two departures from the brief's three listed files: run_pin_tests.rs and tests/refusal_corpus.rs also changed (test-only). The reasons are under open_issues. Athena's recorded fmt and clippy runs, and my own `cargo test --locked --no-fail-fast` (exit 0), passed. I did not run the corpus against past readings, so "0% newly refused" is by construction: the scanned set is a subset of the old one.

open_issues: Departure from the reading's deliverables, test-only: crates/athena-core/src/run_pin_tests.rs. The end-to-end test asserted the old summary refusal and would have failed. It now puts the word in a content criterion, and a twin test shows a summary word is accepted.

Departure from the reading's deliverables, test-only: crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs gains the `boundary-word` input form (17 forms) and four cases (summary and assumption accepted, deliverable path and content criterion refused by `check_boundary_and_repo_files`).

Open question for the user: the title, summary and criterion texts reach landing commit messages (run/close.rs) and the pull request title (run/mod.rs, gh/early.rs). No scan covers those. This change removes the only gate on that text, and the docs and D153 say so without claiming a backstop. Proposed follow-up job: run that text through `athena_context::briefs::plain_boundary_text` at those sinks, with a test that a landing message and pull request title pass `boundary_scan`.

Criterion kind is an imperfect signal, recorded in D153's Tradeoff. A content criterion that only describes a document is still scanned. A behavior criterion that quotes output is not, and the writer's scan and the policy scan at verification catch a word that reaches a tracked file.
The counts of refusals (six on 2026-10-31, two on 2026-10-30) come from the request. Records are absent from the snapshot, so D153 says they were not measured.
mistakes: The first D153 draft began its Decision with the word 'Amends', which the decisions-log parser read as a supersession phrase with no target id and failed the athena-cli backtest test. I reworded it to 'Narrows' and reran the test.
learnings: The athena-cli backtest test `the_real_log_has_no_condition_a_finding_against_the_confirmed_list` parses docs/decisions.md for the supersession phrases ('amends', 'supersedes', 'superseded by') and fails on one with no target id. A new decision entry must not use those words in prose such as 'Amends the word part'.
xtask/tests/policy.rs reads tracked files only; a changed tracked file is scanned, a new file is not.
`cargo test --locked` stops at the first failing test binary, so later crates are not run. `--no-fail-fast` runs them all.
The full suite can run longer than 20 minutes here (the foreground run hit the 1200s limit and moved to the background; it exited 0).

The reader prompts under crates/athena-context/prompts contain no line saying every reading field is scanned for boundary words (grep for 'boundary scan', 'boundary word', 'banned word' found nothing).
desires: A way to read a background command's output file, or a wait tool. Reading outside the working directory is denied, so I could not poll the backgrounded suite.
